newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine government, labor postpone talks to next week.
newsitem.headline: Argentine government, labor postpone talks to next week.

text.p: The Argentine government has postponed until Jan 29 a meeting with union leaders originally planned for Thursday to try to reach consensus over planned labor reforms.

Armando Cavallieri, an executive with the leading CGT labor federation, told reporters the government was likely awaiting the outcome of a new court decision Tuesday on its decrees implementing the reforms.

After the CGT on December 26 led its third general strike of last year, President Carlos Menem signed three decrees reducing union control of collective pay bargaining. They were struck down by the courts but the government has appealed.
Other reforms, such as replacing redundancy payouts with unemployment insurance, are more palatable to the unions and were to be thrashed out in Congress.
The Peronist government and the CGT agreed last week to resume dialogue.
Menem, who faces tough mid-term elections in Congress in October, argues that only the "flexibilization" of labor laws can help reduce a 17.3 percent unemployment rate.
But the unions fear he means to reduce their power and take away worker rights.
On Tuesday night, Argentina's Group of Eight business lobby also agreed to begin talks with trade unions aimed at reaching consensus on the reforms.
